bib.title: Foundations of Large Language Models, Chapter 2: Generative Models

read.skipped: nothing; the chapter text ends at the Summary with no reference list in this file (citations only inline)

question: What are the basic concepts of generative LLMs, how are they trained at scale, and how are they adapted to long contexts?
contributions: General introduction to LLMs: decoder-only Transformer, pre-training, instruction fine-tuning, alignment (SFT, RLHF), prompting
Large-scale training: data preparation, model modifications, distributed training, scaling laws
Long-sequence modeling: hardware optimisations, efficient architectures, KV cache and memory, head/layer sharing, position extrapolation and interpolation

limits: Textbook chapter: almost no experiments of its own; numbers come from other work or are illustrative.
Authors state it is general, not comprehensive; RLHF/PPO and advanced prompting deferred to later chapters; no exhaustive literature review.
Fig 2.4 data points are illustrative only.
Table 2.3 token counts depend on tokenizer and may include repeated sampling of data.
Model table is a late-2024/early-2025 snapshot (Qwen3, DeepSeek-V3, Llama 3.1); test-time compute is mentioned in one sentence only.

Table 2.2 values look wrong in places (outside-knowledge check, unverified in the text): Gemma2 listed as 37B (released size is 27B), and Llama2-70B, Falcon and Mistral-7B listed with equal Q/KV heads although they are reported elsewhere to use GQA/MQA. Verify before citing.
practices: Use pre-norm (F(LNorm(x))+x) for deep LLMs; most are pre-norm (2.2.2.1).
Prefer SwiGLU/GeGLU FFN activations over ReLU in wide FFNs (2.2.2.2).
Remove bias terms to improve training stability (2.2.2.3).
Filter and clean web data; heuristic filtering can discard most of it (2.2.1).
Include code and multilingual data for diversity; code helps reasoning (2.2.1).
Compute SFT loss on the output segment only (2.1.3, Eq 2.18).
Train reward models on ranked comparisons rather than scalar ratings, since ratings are hard to annotate consistently (2.1.4).
Add few-shot demonstrations or chain-of-thought steps, or 'Let's think step by step', for multi-step reasoning (2.1.5).
Combine data, tensor and pipeline parallelism; naive model parallelism leaves devices idle (2.2.3).
Use mixed precision but watch non-associativity of floating-point accumulation across many nodes (2.2.3).
Use GQA to trade KV cache size against expressiveness via ng (2.3.4).
Prefer relative or rotary position schemes over learned absolute embeddings for length generalisation; fine-tune on longer sequences after pre-training (2.3.5, 2.3.6.2).
Use position interpolation or NTK-aware base scaling to extend RoPE models (2.3.5.4).
Do not rely on perplexity alone to evaluate long-context LLMs; use synthetic retrieval tasks and long-input NLP tasks, and beware prompt sensitivity (2.3.6.3).

terms.definition: estimate the probability of a token sequence, factorised by the chain rule Pr(x0..xm)=prod Pr(xi|x0..xi-1)
stack of L blocks, each self-attention + FFN sub-layer, causal mask, softmax over vocabulary on top
post-norm: LNorm(F(input)+input); pre-norm: F(LNorm(input))+input
fine-tune pre-trained LLM on (instruction, response) pairs; loss computed on the output segment only
guiding LLMs to behave in ways that accord with human values and goals
continuing training of pre-trained LLMs on new, task-oriented, labelled data
learn a reward model from human comparisons of outputs, then fine-tune the policy against it with RL (e.g. PPO)
-E log Sigmoid(R(x,yk1)-R(x,yk2)) over human-preferred pairs
the entire input to an LLM; used interchangeably with model input
demonstrate ways to solve problems in the prompt and condition predictions on them
demonstrate intermediate problem-solving steps in the prompt; zero-shot CoT appends 'Let's think step by step.'
only rescales by root mean square, no re-centering; used in Llama
GeLU: h*Phi(h); GLU: sigma(hW1+b1) * (hW2+b2); GeGLU uses GeLU, SwiGLU uses Swish; PaLM and Llama use SwiGLU
split minibatch; split layers; split a weight matrix; split batch into micro-batches overlapping across workers
relation between performance and model size, compute and data; basic form L(x)=a x^b (+ irreducible error)
abilities that appear when model size is scaled to a certain level (Wei et al. 2022b)
stored keys and values of previous tokens during autoregressive inference; grows linearly with sequence length
attend only to a subset G of positions; weights renormalised over G
kernel feature map phi replaces softmax, giving recurrent summaries mu_i and nu_i, constant cost per step
MQA shares one K,V across all heads; GQA shares K,V within ng groups
first few tokens kept in attention to absorb excessive attention scores and stabilise long context
interpolate LM distribution with distribution from k nearest hidden states in a datastore: lambda*Pr_knn + (1-lambda)*Pr_lm
retrieve k chunks for context x and build x' = g(c1..ck, x) via a prompt template
rotary positional embedding: rotate token embedding by position-dependent angle so dot product depends on t-s
map positions in [0,m] into trained range [0,ml]
scale RoPE base b by lambda=(m/ml)^(d/(d-2))

code.snippet: Pr(x0,...,xm) = prod_{i=0..m} Pr(xi | x0,...,xi-1);  log Pr = sum_i log Pr(xi | x0,...,xi-1)
post-norm: output = LNorm(F(input) + input); pre-norm: output = F(LNorm(input)) + input
LNorm(h) = alpha ⊙ (h - mu)/(sigma + eps) + beta;  RMSNorm(h) = alpha ⊙ h/(sigma_rms + eps)
GLU(h) = sigma(hW1+b1) ⊙ (hW2+b2); SwiGLU uses Swish(h)=h ⊙ Sigmoid(ch)
linear PI: Ro'(xi, i*theta) = Ro(xi, (ml/m) i*theta); NTK-aware: lambda = (m/ml)^(d/(d-2)), theta' uses (lambda*b)
